stem: Transition metal atoms and transition metal ions form complexes by combining with species called ligands.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
When $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ is added to an aqueous solution containing $[\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ a precipitation reaction occurs accompanied by a colour change.

In this reaction two of the water ligands each lose one $\text{H}^+$ ion. The $\text{H}^+$ ions are gained by $\text{OH}^-$ ions from the $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State the colour change seen in this precipitation reaction.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Complete the ionic equation for this precipitation reaction.

$$[\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+} + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
This precipitation reaction can also be described as a different type of reaction.

Name this type of reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
L is an uncharged tridentate ligand. L donates three lone pairs to a metal atom or ion.

Cobalt forms an octahedral complex ion, E, with L. Complex ion E has a 2+ charge.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the oxidation state of cobalt in E.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The d-orbitals of the cobalt atom or ion present in E are split in energy.

State the number of d-orbitals that are at a higher energy level and the number of d-orbitals that are at a lower energy level.

| number of d-orbitals at a higher energy level |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| number of d-orbitals at a lower energy level |  |

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
The mineral chromite contains a compound which has the formula $\text{FeCr}_n\text{O}_4$. The oxidation state of iron in $\text{FeCr}_n\text{O}_4$ is +2.

A sample of $4.18\text{ g}$ of $\text{FeCr}_n\text{O}_4$ is dissolved in an excess of sulfuric acid. The resulting solution is made up to $250\text{ cm}^3$. This is solution F.

All the $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions in $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ of solution F are oxidised to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions by exactly $18.7\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$.

One $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ion reacts with five $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions. Assume no other oxidation reaction occurs.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions with $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ions in acid solution.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions in $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ of solution F.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the $M_{\text{r}}$ of $\text{FeCr}_n\text{O}_4$ and use your answer to deduce the value of $n$.
